description.narrative: KSP aims to support sustainable urban development in Kenya primarily through an exchange of expertise, knowledge and experiences between Kenyan and Swedish actors. It will implement the Swedish inspired concept for urban sustainability - Symbiocity Approach – which has also been successfully implemented with modification in various countries in the world. The project will be anchored at the Council of Governors, which will coordinate the project on behalf of counties. The Swedish Association and Regions (SALAR) will provide technical assistance and linkages with Swedish actors based on experience gained implementing similar projects across the world. In addition to strengthening the coordination role of the CoG, the project will build sustainable urban development planning capacity within the CoG and counties. It will also pilot interventions in at least 7 counties using the Symbiocity approach. Based on lessons learnt from the pilots, the project will expand capacity building activities to all the 47 counties. In the process, the project will build the institutional capacity of CoG, strengthen counties’ capacity for planning and implementing project using a sustainability perspective and improve access to infrastructure and services in selected counties. Ultimately, it is expected that the project will contribute to improved conditions for urban residents in Kenya.

Kenya SymbioCity Programmet (KSP) syftar till att stödja hållbar urban utveckling i Kenya, huvud-sakligen genom att kenyanska och svenska aktörer utbyter expertis, kunskaper och erfaren¬heter. Det är det svenskinspirerade konceptet för urban hållbarhet – SymbioCity – som ska genomföras, och som i olika modifierade former framgångsrikt genomförts i flera länder runt om i världen. Projektet kommer att genomföras tillsammans med Council of Governors (CoG, som är de lokala regeringschefernas högsta råd och en officiell lagstiftad institution som representerar samtliga 47 Länsregeringar), som ska koordinera projektet för och med länsregeringarna, genom CoG:s specifika projektkontor (PIU) och genom Kommittén för Urban Utveckling på CoG. Projektkontoret kommer att hantera finansiellt och tekninskt stöd till länen, men inte kanalisera medel vidare till länen i denna första insatsperiod. Sveriges Kommuner och Landsting (SKL) kommer att bidra med teknisk assistans till CoG och länen och dessutom förmedla kontakter med svenska aktörer utifrån erfarenheter från genomföranden av liknande projekt runtom i världen. Utöver att stärka CoG:s koordinerande roll kommer projektet att leda till att det byggs upp planeringskapacitet för en hållbar urban utveckling vid CoG och hos länsregeringarna (som alla är representerade genom CoG). Pilotprojekt som utgår från förhållningssättet SymbioCity kommer att genomföras i minst sju regioner. Utifrån de lärdomar som dras av pilotprojekten kommer det sedan att genomföras kapacitetsuppbyggande aktiviteter i alla de 47 regionerna. Under processen kommer det att byggas upp institutionell kapacitet hos CoG, samtidigt som kapaciteten för att - utifrån ett hållbarhets¬perspektiv - planera och genomföra projekt kommer att stärkas, samt att tillgången till infrastruktur och tjänster i de utvalda regionerna ökar. Slutligen förväntas projektet bidra till förbättrade levnadsvillkor och möjligheter för urbana invånare i Kenya.

The overall goal of the programme was to contribute to "Inclusive, innovative and sustainable urban development planning in Kenya". The intermediary programme objective was "Urban development stakeholders have increased capacity and ability to guide Kenyan urban development in a more sustainable direction".
Supporting the intermediary programme objective were four objectives: 1) CoG is set up to be responsive to counties needs and support urban planning, management and development: This would be achieved through institutional development activities and knowledge transfer from the experienced SALAR. A particular focus was the creation and or strengthening of a technical unit to support the Urban Development Committee.
2) Local stakeholders in seven counties plan, manage and develop their localities with a sustainable perspective: This would be achieved through the piloting of the SymbioCity Approach in a real urban local setting, leading to a needs analysis through the urban sustainability review process and development urban visions to be taken further by the county. Piloting of urban improvements according to SymbioCity approach principles was also included in this objective.
3) MoLHUD/UDD and CoG have increased capacity to support urban planning, management and development in counties: This entailed institutional development activities coupled with improved collaboration between MoLHUD and CoG for supporting sustainable urban planning, development and management, in line with the national urban development policy.
4) Kenya SymbioCity Programme experiences shared among counties and urban development stakeholders to stimulate cross fertilization and networking: This objective would be achieved through the networking and interaction with other projects and organisations, which would help disseminate SymbioCity expertise and experience.

description.narrative:
Summary of results
Institutional strengthening - the Council of Governors (CoG) established and sustained a technical urban planning support function, including dedicated planning expertise to support the Land, Planning and Urban Development Committee. - key programme staff, including the Project Manager, were absorbed into permanent positions within CoG, helping retain institutional knowledge and technical capacity. - strategic planning tools were developed, including: Planning Our Towns Toolkit, Urban Sustainability Reviews (USRs), Place Making Guide, County Spatial Planning Guidelines. - increased institutional capacity within CoG to support counties on urban planning and development. - planning tools are being used beyond the programme, for example by Kitui Municipality and national urban planning initiatives. - improved urban infrastructure and services.
Across the seven pilot counties, the programme completed Quick Wins and larger Change Projects that delivered improved drainage systems, improved solid waste management, rainwater harvesting systems, improved sanitation facilities, market upgrading, ecotoilets, public lighting, green public spaces, tree planting, public parks, market infrastructure, improved water access and community recreational facilities.
Examples of outcomes include: reduced flooding through drainage improvements, improved access to clean water, improved sanitation, enhanced market trading conditions, increased business opportunities, improved security through lighting, increased environmental awareness, greener and more attractive public spaces, improved waste collection and recycling practices.
Community participation and governance - urban sustainability reviews were developed through extensive stakeholder engagement. - communities participated in identifying priorities and designing interventions. - community champions, liaison officers and environmental champions were established. - increased local ownership of projects. - strengthened cooperation between county departments. - improved collaboration between government and communities. - formation of community based organisations supporting waste management and environmental stewardship. - environmental sustainability.
The programme contributed to: urban greening, increased tree cover, improved waste management, composting and recycling, rainwater harvesting, protection of public spaces, improved drainage and storm water management, and increased environmental awareness among communities.
County ownership Many counties committed resources for: - operation and maintenance of infrastructure - staffing of new facilities - maintenance of drainage, lighting and water systems, waste management - continued funding through county budgets.
Examples include Kitui, Kakamega, Homa Bay and Nakuru counties.
Financial sustainability Five of the seven pilot counties integrated SymbioCity priorities into their County Integrated Development Plans (CIDPs), creating opportunities to continue financing interventions beyond the programme period.
Community sustainability Community ownership was strengthened through community champions, environmental champions, tree adoption initiatives, waste management groups and continuous community participation.
The programme successfully demonstrated the value of integrated, participatory urban planning through pilot interventions in seven counties and strengthened the institutional capacity of the Council of Governors (CoG) to support urban development. The programme also generated practical planning tools, methodologies and lessons that have potential for wider application beyond the pilot counties.
Overall, Sida assesses that the programme has achieved satisfactory results and has contributed to improved urban planning capacity and more sustainable urban development practices within participating counties
